summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 7/17)

data.turoyo: Mede layt gabi d mbaxbašnox, d ubenox ḥoṯi.
data.translation: ich habe gar nichts, was ich dir schenken könnte; ich will dir meine Schwester zur Frau geben

rationale: New Infectum box; first-person form with recipient suffix inside a relative clause.

data.turoyo: Qrelale, lwəšle ǧule w aṯi l qum u paša. Ḥəlle ebe lu paša, omər: “Alo xort kayiso yo, hano waǧəb di ʕaskar yo, elo mbaxbašliləxyo.”
data.translation: Da legte jener seine Kleider an und trat vor den Statthalter; dieser betrachtete ihn und sagte: »Warlich, es ist ein schöner Jüngling; der passt zum Soldaten, aber ich habe ihn dir zum Geschenk gemacht«.

rationale: Fills Preterit sense 1; recipient -ləx and final -yo contrast with the inherited -lox declaration.

summary: All three tokens fit existing sense 1 schenken, bestechen; only the gift component is attested here. The absence of bribery in this small set does not justify deleting the inherited gloss.
Keep the entry’s stem I label for the quadriliteral-looking loan. Initial m- does not by itself license relabelling the entry as II, III or Q.

Preterit gift declarations function performatively at PrS 3/23 and 4/15. Infectum mbaxbašnox occurs in a relative clause under absence of available gift material; the edition’s possibility wording need not be an independent mood or sense.
Valency includes zero-marked human gift theme Ḥalime and recipient -lox, recipient -ləx plus a final -yo element, and the Infectum contracted recipient ending. Exact analysis of -yo remains open.
The inherited Kurdish source is consistent with a lexical loan verb. There is no separate light verb plus noun construction or new idiom to add.
Reconcile inherited prs 10/2 with supplied PrS 3/23; the same Ḥalime declaration has not been duplicated.
Is final -yo in mbaxbašliləxyo an anaphoric patient element or a copular reinforcement? Confirm the suffix sequence from speakers.
At PrS 7/17, is the possibility reading supplied by the relative construction or by the discourse context?
